gap: No result ChatGPT got states a single measured figure for any laptop screen extender: the two cited pages I could open say they work from published specs. The only named measurements I could open are for older models from two brands in our table: Notebookcheck measured a FOPO 12-inch dual-screen extender at 193.1 cd/m² peak and 247:1 contrast, and Parka Blogs measured the Mobile Pixels Duex Plus at 152 nits and 68% sRGB.
standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com under-$200 (cited) and itechguides.com 2025 guide (cited); deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403. Both opened pages state they are 'based on published specifications' / 'not hands-on testing', and every nits, contrast and weight figure on them is a listing claim. Neither cites RTINGS, Notebookcheck, Tom's Hardware or PCMag. So any named measurement is new against them. I scored it 1 rather than 2 because I found no named measurement for any current under-$200 candidate itself (FOPO S1, FOPO S7, Mobile Pixels Fold, Mobile Pixels Glance, UPERFECT 14" 2K, Arzopa E1, Laptomo, SIAVIALA). The two measurements I opened are on 2022 units of older models, so they support a caution and cannot rank the candidates.
decides: It does not change the pick. It confirms the pick should rest on video path, fit range and price, not on claimed brightness. It supports one honest sentence on the page: the 250–300 nit claims in this class are makers' figures, no named lab has measured the screens on this page, and the two older units from these brands that were measured came in under 200 nits (Notebookcheck on FOPO's 12-inch at 193.1 cd/m², Parka Blogs on the Duex Plus at 152 nits). That is a reason not to rank FOPO S1 against S7 or the Fold on brightness claims, and to say plainly that Dealectric does not test units.
candidates: Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS (just over $200)

findings.product: FOPO 12-inch dual-screen lid-mounted extender (2022 model, not the S1 or S7)
findings.label: Peak brightness, measured by Notebookcheck (Allen Ngo)
findings.source_title: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender review: Clunky and more fragile than standalone portable monitors (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Review published 2022-07-23; instrument X-Rite i1Pro 2; test laptop 2022 HP Pavilion Plus 14. 'Triple' in the title means the laptop plus two added 12-inch 1080p screens. Older, smaller model than the S1 and S7 in our table, so it is a class and brand datapoint only. FOPO's spec for the S1 and S7 is 250 cd/m² (our records).

findings.label: Contrast and black level, measured by Notebookcheck
findings.note: Published 2022-07-23, X-Rite i1Pro 2. FOPO's spec for the S1 and S7 is 1000:1 (our records); this measurement is on a different, older panel.

findings.label: Response time and PWM, measured by Notebookcheck
findings.value: 29.2 ms black-to-white; 31.6 ms grey-to-grey; no PWM at any brightness level
findings.note: Published 2022-07-23. Notebookcheck's headline verdict: 'Clunky and more fragile than standalone portable monitors'.

findings.label: Video path as Notebookcheck ran it
findings.value: Each screen has two USB-C ports (one power-in, one power plus video) and one mini-HDMI. A laptop with two video-capable USB-C ports needs one USB-C cable per screen; over HDMI each screen needs a separate power cable. Windows sees the two as ordinary external displays.
findings.note: Matches this page's rule of one video-capable port per added screen on driver-free FOPO duals. The review does not name DisplayPort Alt Mode or any driver.

findings.product: Mobile Pixels Duex Plus 13.3-inch (older sibling of the Duex Max DS)
findings.label: Brightness and colour gamut, measured by Parka Blogs (Teoh Yi Chie)
findings.source_title: Review: Duex Plus portable display attachment for laptops (Parka Blogs)
findings.note: Published 2022-07-12. Quote: 'With a colour calibrator, I measured colour support for just 68% sRGB and a maximum brightness of 152 nits.' The calibrator model is not named; the unit was supplied by Mobile Pixels. Not the 14.1-inch Duex Max DS in our table, which is over the $200 line at $215.99.

findings.label: Named review, no instrument measurements
findings.value: Camera Jabber reports no measured nits, gamut or contrast. It observed that a 16-inch MacBook Pro M1 'maintained power for a good three hours' of photo editing and writing with the Glance on USB-C. Listed weight 0.95 kg.
findings.note: Published 2023-03-26, byline Camera Jabber Team; the variant is not named. The reviewer says the colour space 'doesn't cover Adobe RGB or P3' and that it is not for precise colour work. The weight is from the spec list, not weighed.

RTINGS' measurements for the Mobile Pixels Trio and Duex Plus: both review pages (rtings.com/monitor/reviews/mobile-pixels/trio and /duex-plus) returned only title and breadcrumbs. Gadget Review's Trio page prints a table (241 nits, 979:1, 69.4% sRGB, 25.1 ms input lag) without naming who measured it, and contradicts itself (241, 261 and 240 nits), so it is not used.
Notebookcheck's colour-gamut figures for the FOPO 12-inch: the page summary returned 79% sRGB and 79% AdobeRGB, which cannot both be right, so gamut is left out.
Any named-lab measurement (brightness, contrast, gamut, weight, power draw) for the FOPO S1 or S7: searched Notebookcheck, RTINGS, Tom's Hardware and PCMag and found none.
Any named-lab measurement for the Mobile Pixels Fold (15.6-inch 1080p or 16-inch QHD): search returned only maker and retailer specs.
Any named-lab measurement for the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS: the root-nation.com review returned 403, no PCMag review turned up, and Amateur Photographer's Duex Max review appeared in snippets only.

Any named-lab measurement for the UPERFECT 14-inch 2K extender, Arzopa E1 dual 15.6-inch, Laptomo 15.6-inch detachable or SIAVIALA 14-inch: only retailer listings were found, and UPERFECT listings conflict on brightness (300 vs 400 nits) and resolution (2240×1400 vs 2160×1440).
